messages:
jessica-cs: FYI ACME reported new hires created via SCIM but no roles are being applied. They said this was working until an Okta change yesterday.

tom-customer: Users show as Active in our org but role field is empty. This is breaking access to multiple internal apps.

provisioning-bot: provisioning event: POST /scim/v2/Users 201 created -> userId: 0a1b2c3d

jessica-cs: I grabbed our SCIM audit logs. When we try to PATCH group membership to map to a role we see a 403. Snippet: 
```
[2026-02-18T14:21:03Z] PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/0f9a... - 403 - \"insufficient_scope: scim:write:groups required\"
[2026-02-18T14:21:03Z] auth.token_id=acct_scim_9876
```

mateo-eng: That message screams token scope. Which token is the Okta provisioning app using on their side?

tom-customer: Okta is using our Provisioning API token. We didn't rotate it, but we did change an admin role in Okta yesterday.

ida-sre: Quick check in our Admin Console -> acct_scim_9876 only has scopes: `read:users`, `read:groups`. No write scopes are present. That matches the 403 on group writes.

jessica-cs: So Okta can create users but can't add them to role-backed groups. That explains active users without roles.

mateo-eng: Remediation / repro steps I used:
1) Get a provisioning token with scopes `scim:write:users` and `scim:write:groups` (customer to rotate in Okta).
2) Trigger our reconcile endpoint: `POST /internal/scim/reconcile?org_id=acme` authenticated with an admin token.
3) Watch for successful PATCH 200 responses for Groups.

ida-sre: CS can pass this curl to the customer for step 2 (placeholder URL):
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/internal/scim/reconcile?org_id=acme" \\
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>" \\
 -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

jessica-cs: If they can't rotate token immediately, we can do a Console CSV bulk assign as a stopgap to restore role membership.

mateo-eng: Also filing an engineering task to make the 403 actionable: ENG-plat-1123 to include missing scopes in the error (e.g. `insufficient_scope: missing [scim:write:groups]`) returned from our token validation.

tom-customer: Created a new token in Okta: acct_scim_1122 with scopes `read:users, write:users, read:groups, write:groups` and updated the Okta provisioning app to use it.

okta-bot: provisioning event: Bearer token rotated by Tom (okta-admin)

ida-sre: Ran a dry reconcile using acct_scim_1122 — group PATCH calls returned 200 and we applied role assignments for 127 users.

jessica-cs: Tom, can you confirm a few impacted users now show roles? Which user ids were failing earlier?

tom-customer: Affected ids were 0a1b2c3d, 0a1b2c3e, 0a1b2c4f. Two of three show roles now; one still missing due to an externalId mismatch in the group mapper.

mateo-eng: For that one-off I patched the group membership directly:
```
PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/{groupId}
Content-Type: application/scim+json
Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>

{ "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"], "Operations": [ { "op": "add", "path": "members", "value": [{ "value": "0a1b2c4f" }] } ] }
```

jessica-cs: After reconcile + the one-off patch Tom confirms all 128 users have the correct role mappings. They validated app access — everything green.

tom-customer: Really appreciate the rapid help. Agreed we need clearer errors when tokens lack scopes — wasted a fair bit of time.

mateo-eng: ENG-plat-1123 will update token validation to return the missing scopes in the 403. Also adding a CS playbook entry: /playbooks/scim-token-scope-checklist with steps to check token scopes, rotate token, use reconcile, and fallback CSV.

ida-sre: Closing loop in internal incident notes. If anyone wants raw reconcile logs DM me — I'll strip token values before sharing.

jessica-cs: Marking resolved with customer. :white_check_mark:
